clue.text: Pay attention, for example, to product of grapevine

parts.note: to pay attention to someone is to hear them out
say is used like 'for example' when offering an instance

explanation.surface: An instruction to heed some example of gossip passed along the grapevine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The grapevine' is the informal network through which rumours spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumour heard second-hand is exactly what the grapevine produces, so the phrase describes unverified gossip.

clue.text: Mix sulphur with ash to produce flowers

indicators.note: to mix is to jumble together, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: combine sulphur with wood ash to grow blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantain lilies, shade-loving garden plants, flower as well as being grown for their leaves.

clue.text: Unpaid wife left, not getting on

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter for wife goes away

parts.note: an unpaid worker is wageless

explanation.surface: An unwaged wife walks out, the marriage not working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on' means growing old, not getting along.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never seems to grow old is not getting on in years.

clue.text: Rewrite poor clues for extremely cold but not freezing

indicators.note: an instruction to rewrite, so the letters are set down again in another order

explanation.surface: Advice to a setter to redraft weak clues about coldness.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercooled liquid is chilled below its freezing point yet stays liquid.

clue.text: Pull rabbit out of stetson finally?

indicators.note: read as outside of, so rabbit's synonym surrounds the next piece

parts.note: rabbit is British slang for chatter, as is yak

indicators.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A conjuror finally pulling a rabbit out of a cowboy hat.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a sudden sharp tug is to pull hard.

clue.text: I am left behind in hopeless difficulty

parts.note: contracted, I am becomes I'M
something passé has been left behind by fashion, out of date

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned by others finds themselves in a desperate fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock or dead end is a predicament with no way forward, a hopeless difficulty.

clue.text: In dialect name changes are fortuitous

indicators.note: changes means alters, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that words changing in local speech is a matter of chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring by chance as a side matter, so happening fortuitously.

clue.text: Insistence on correctness is pointless in Jewish festival

indicators.note: lacking a compass point, so S for south is dropped

parts.note: purism is strict insistence on correctness

explanation.surface: Pedantry has no place at a Jewish celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring festival celebrating the Jews' deliverance in the Book of Esther.

clue.text: In South Africa, encountered a new composer

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: Meeting a fresh composer while in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was a Czech composer, best known for Má vlast.

clue.text: Elders no longer keeping motorway limits?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the trees surround the next piece

parts.note: elders are trees
M is a motorway in Britain, as in M1

explanation.surface: Former elders guarding the edges of a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elders' looks like senior people; it is the elder tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The furthest points or outer bounds of something are its limits.

clue.text: It enables travellers to go flat out

definitions.text: It enables travellers to go flat out

parts.words: It enables travellers to go flat out
parts.note: 'go flat out' suggests top speed, but here means lying flat to rest on a train journey

explanation.surface: Something that lets travellers reach maximum speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage with berths lets passengers lie down flat while travelling overnight.

clue.text: Munch to do etching?

definitions.meaning: to munch is to chew and consume food
in etching, acid corrodes or bites into the metal plate

explanation.surface: The painter Munch apparently turning his hand to etching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Munch' looks like the Norwegian painter Edvard Munch, which pulls toward art; it is the verb for chewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Munching is chewing food, and acid in etching corrodes the plate, both senses of the same verb.

clue.text: Deaf artist upset, once frightened

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist who cannot hear is distressed and scared.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or dialect word for afraid, hence 'once' marking it as old usage for frightened.

clue.text: A reservoir selling water

parts.note: a dam holds back a reservoir, and the word can stand for the reservoir itself
a sale is an act of selling

explanation.surface: A water company flogging off one of its reservoirs.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular old name for plain drinking water, the only drink of the first man.

clue.text: In rank, irritating little thing almost making no progress

indicators.note: in means the next piece goes inside rank's synonym

parts.note: station means rank or standing

indicators.note: almost means not quite whole, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a gnat is a small irritating insect

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in their position, pestered by a small annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a state of standing still, with no development or progress being made.

clue.text: Start to slow, blowing horn, and stop large car

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

parts.note: hooting is sounding a car horn
to brake is to stop a vehicle

explanation.surface: Driving instructions: slow down, sound the horn and halt the big car.
explanation.walkthrough: A shooting brake is an old British name for an estate car (station wagon).
explanation.definitionFit: A dated British term for an estate car, a roomy car with a rear door for luggage.

clue.text: Appointment that lacks recognition

parts.note: a meeting arranged between strangers, who will not recognise each other

explanation.surface: An appointment to a post that goes unacknowledged.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic meeting between two people who have never met each other before.

clue.text: A choice including diamonds for acceptance

indicators.note: including means containing, so the outer pieces hold the next one

parts.note: an option is a choice
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A selection that includes diamonds, as if picking an engagement ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Adopting an idea or proposal is taking it on, a form of acceptance.

clue.text: One glass on top of another: that's the way to keep out the cold!

definitions.text: One glass on top of another: that's the way to keep out the cold!

parts.words: One glass on top of another: that's the way to keep out the cold!
parts.note: reads like drinking glass after glass to warm up, but means two panes of window glass for insulation

explanation.surface: A drinker's advice that another glassful will keep the chill away.
explanation.definitionFit: Windows with two panes of glass and a gap between them insulate a house against cold.

clue.text: Plump teenagers: you can find any number

indicators.note: you can find signals that letters are sitting within the words

explanation.surface: Plump teenagers are everywhere you look.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for very many, an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: Good to run down crescent

parts.note: rowing, as in scolding, is running someone down

explanation.surface: A good street to jog along, a crescent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crescent' looks like a curved street; it is the Latin-derived adjective meaning increasing, as of the waxing moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Crescent comes from Latin crescere, to grow, so a crescent moon is a waxing one.

clue.text: Plastered with jewels

explanation.surface: Drunk and dripping with gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned is slang for intoxicated, and a ring can be stoned, set with gemstones.

clue.text: Epic play represented the making of a churchwarden

indicators.note: represented means presented anew, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A grand drama staged to show how a church officer is appointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges EPIC PLAY. A churchwarden is also a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe, which is what the white clay makes; the stray '5' in the held clue is an OCR artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine white clay is the material from which long clay tobacco pipes called churchwardens are made.

clue.text: Inexpensive sort of skate?

definitions.meaning: the word that comes before skate to make the name for a miser

explanation.surface: A bargain skate.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpensive goods are low-priced, and a cheapskate is a stingy person.

clue.text: Apt fuss about first sign of roguish sex appeal

indicators.note: about means around, so the fuss is put around the next piece

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone apt to make a fuss over a rogue's attractiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt in the sense of skilful or clever, which is what adroit means.

clue.text: Hobble, though not stiff

explanation.surface: Walking awkwardly despite no stiffness.
explanation.definitionFit: To limp is to walk unevenly from injury, and something limp is floppy.

clue.text: That's used to keep cold

parts.note: something put to work keeping drinks or food chilled

explanation.surface: Describing what keeps things chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water is the familiar coolant for chilling drinks and preserving food.

clue.text: Reversed 1500m-equivalent race heat results?

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so this piece is read backwards

parts.note: the 1500m is the metric mile, so it equates to I MILE, one mile
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: Results from the heats of a track race run the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversed' turns I MILE into ELIMI. Heats are preliminary rounds in which runners are knocked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualifying heats knock out the slower runners, so their outcome is the removal of competitors.

clue.text: Skittles out with this sort of bowling

definitions.text: Skittles out with this sort of bowling

parts.words: Skittles out with this sort of bowling
parts.note: a style of skittles in which nine targets are set up to be knocked down

explanation.surface: Bowling that knocks every skittle down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepin bowling is a traditional form of skittles played with nine pins.

clue.text: Toast daughter getting engaged

parts.note: to pledge someone is to drink their health, a toast

explanation.surface: A father toasts his daughter on her engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pledged in marriage means promised to someone, betrothed.
